title: LCLI-723 round-1 follow-ups: the undeclared-Story carve-out test, 0.2's every-type enum scope, and the untested base.fields empty-enum site
description:
Non-blocking findings from the LCLI-723 review (approved at 10cc270e; PR opum-ai/lore-cli#586). None blocked the merge; all three are gaps in what the change PROVES or SAYS, not defects in what it does.

(2) test/effective-status-enum.test.ts:108 — "the 0.1 task-rollup carve-out survives the precedence change" runs against `customProfile("0.1")`, which declares ONLY `ADR`. A `type: "Story"` document is therefore an UNKNOWN type in that profile, and the carve-out return it exercises is the unknown-type one, not the ADR check: the test proves the carve-out holds for a type the profile does not declare, which is a weaker claim than its name makes. Fix either way — declare a Story in `customProfile("0.1")` and assert the three rollup values pass on a DECLARED type (preferred: that is the claim the name makes), or rename the test to what it actually proves. Note the 0.2 sibling at :47 in the LCLI-669 file uses the BUILT-IN profile, where Story IS declared, so the two files currently demonstrate the carve-out at different strengths.

(3) On OKF 0.2, `validateLifecycleStatus` (src/core/schema.ts:483) judges EVERY type by that type's effective enum; the ADR-only restriction is the 0.1 carve-out, not the 0.2 rule. LCLI-723 made that enum the profile's DECLARED one, so the scope statement is now load-bearing for a custom profile's non-ADR types too. The CHANGELOG's LCLI-723 entry says the change applies "on OKF 0.1 and 0.2 alike" but never states that 0.2's scope is every type. Add one line. MEASURE the sentence against the pinned capacities before landing it: `docs/reference/cli-surface.md` and `cli-contract.md` are declared by several `.lore/agents/*.toml` profiles, and `reference/cli-contract` is PINNED by implementation, review and verification — a CHANGELOG sentence is free (CHANGELOG.md is not a declared source), so put it there and leave the reference pages alone.

(5) NARROWED BY MEASUREMENT, 2026-10-14 — the review reported "no empty-enum load test, although assertNonEmptyEnum exists". There ARE two: test/profile.test.ts:307 pins `types[0].fields.status.enum` and :318 pins a list's `items.enum`. `assertNonEmptyEnum` also refuses at the third declaration site, verified by calling `parseProfile` directly:

    type field enum=[]        -> t: types[0].fields.status.enum must not be empty
    base.fields enum=[]       -> t: base.fields.status.enum must not be empty
    items enum=[]             -> t: types[0].fields.tags.items.enum must not be empty

So the residual gap is the `[base.fields]` site ALONE: it refuses correctly and no test pins it. Worth pinning rather than the other two, because `effectiveLifecycleStatusEnum` (src/core/profile.ts) reads the BASE `status` spec whenever a type declares none — an empty `[base.fields] status = { enum = [] }` is precisely the input the effective-enum path depends on being refused, and nothing currently holds that line.

NOT IN THIS TASK, and deliberately not changed: `superseded_status` is accepted on ANY type (src/core/profile.ts:530) while DEC-192 (6) says "a key on the ADR type". The leader is taking that to opum-doc; a test should pin whichever way it rules, and it is filed separately once the ruling lands.
plan: (2) test/effective-status-enum.test.ts:108 — declare a Story IN `customProfile("0.1")` and assert the three rollup values pass on a DECLARED type, which is the claim the test's name makes. Today the profile declares only ADR, so `type: "Story"` is an UNKNOWN type there and the carve-out return exercised is the unknown-type one. Keep a companion case for the undeclared type only if it adds a distinct claim; otherwise let the declared one carry it.

(3) CHANGELOG.md — one line in the existing LCLI-723 entry stating that on OKF 0.2 the effective enum governs EVERY type, not only ADRs (the ADR-only restriction is the 0.1 carve-out). CHANGELOG.md is NOT a declared agent-profile source, so this is free; the reference pages are pinned and stay untouched.

(5) test/profile.test.ts — pin the THIRD assertion site, `[base.fields]`. Sites one and two are already pinned at :307 (`types[0].fields.status.enum`) and :318 (`items.enum`); `base.fields.status.enum must not be empty` refuses correctly and nothing holds that line. It matters more than the other two because `effectiveLifecycleStatusEnum` reads the BASE `status` spec whenever a type declares none.

Proofs with mutation controls: revert the declared-Story fixture to an ADR-only profile and confirm the (2) test reddens; remove assertNonEmptyEnum's call and confirm the base.fields test reddens while the two existing sites do too.
Gate the MERGED state (branch cut from origin/dev bb8956d7) and stop at the green head for review.
implementationNotes:
BUILT, 2026-10-14, branch chore/LCLI-728-followups off merged dev bb8956d7. All three items, plus two corrections the work itself turned up.

(2) THE PREFERRED FIX DID NOT WORK AS WRITTEN, and the reason is worth keeping. The item said: declare a Story in `customProfile("0.1")` and assert the three rollup values pass on a DECLARED type. Declaring `Story` alone makes that test FAIL -- but not from `validateLifecycleStatus`. It fails from the generated TYPE SCHEMA: `invalid Story frontmatter: status: Invalid option: expected one of "draft"|"approved"`. The Story inherits the base `status = { enum = ["draft", "approved"] }`, and that schema runs on EVERY OKF version, so a 0.1 task-coupled type whose profile CLOSED its `status` vocabulary has closed its own rollup key -- the schema rejects a rollup value before the lifecycle check is ever consulted. The carve-out is therefore only observable where `status` is OPEN, which is exactly how the built-in profile declares it.
So the fixture now declares `{ name: "Story", fields: { status: {} } }` -- a declared type with its own open `status` -- which isolates the carve-out the test names, and mirrors the built-in profile's own declaration. Both halves are pinned: on 0.1 the three rollup values pass; on 0.2 the SAME declared type is judged against its effective enum (the built-in triple, since its `status` declares no enum) and `done` is refused. The test also asserts `profile.types.has("Story")` as a PRECONDITION, so the fixture cannot silently regress to the undeclared shape that made the old test prove less than its name.
That last point is the generalisable one: a test whose fixture accidentally exercises a FALLBACK path proves the fallback, not the rule. Assert the precondition that makes the test about the rule.

(5) CORRECTION TO MY OWN FILING. I recorded "three declaration sites" for `assertNonEmptyEnum`; that is wrong, and the difference matters to anyone mutating it. It has TWO call sites -- `parseFieldSpec` and `parseItems` -- covering THREE addressable places, because `parseFieldSpec` serves both a type's own `fields` and `[base.fields]`, told apart only by the `where` string. The `[base.fields]` place is the one that was unpinned, and the new test pins it and says so.

MUTATION CONTROLS, two, both reddening the predicted subset. M2 regresses the fixture to the DEFECT's shape (an ADR-only profile): reddens exactly the two carve-out tests, which is the point -- without the precondition assertion the old fixture would have passed while proving the fallback. M3 removes the field-spec guard at the CODE level, since (5)'s fix is a test over existing behaviour: reddens the pre-existing LORE-140 type-field test AND the new `[base.fields]` test -- the two places that one call site serves -- and leaves the `items` test green, which is the separable assertion behaving.

(3) The CHANGELOG line went into the existing LCLI-723 entry: on OKF 0.2 the effective enum governs EVERY type, and the ADR-only reach is the 0.1 carve-out for task-coupled types rather than a rule about 0.2. CHANGELOG.md is not a declared agent-profile source, so it is free; the pinned reference pages were left alone.

GATES on the merged state: bun test 5108 pass / 3 skip / 0 fail (5111 tests, 150 files); typecheck 0; lint 0; `bun run lore check` exit 0, 0 profiles over capacity.

FOLLOW-UP (4), the `superseded_status`-on-any-type question, is CLOSED by DEC-192 (7) -- ratified as built, with its own test and doc line filed on LCLI-729. Nothing in this task changed it.
finalSummary:
All three non-blocking findings from the LCLI-723 review were delivered by PR opum-ai/lore-cli#591, squash f93d5a23, which is an ancestor of origin/dev.

(2) test/effective-status-enum.test.ts declares a Story in the custom profile and asserts profile.types.has("Story") as a PRECONDITION, so the test proves the 0.1 task-rollup carve-out on a DECLARED type rather than on the unknown-type fallback its old fixture accidentally exercised. The fixture declares status OPEN because a closed enum is refused by the generated type schema before the lifecycle check is consulted; the note records why.

(3) The CHANGELOG's LCLI-723 entry now states that on OKF 0.2 the effective enum governs every type's status, and that the ADR-only reach is the 0.1 carve-out for task-coupled types rather than a rule about 0.2. CHANGELOG.md is not a declared agent-profile source, so the line is free.

(5) test/profile.test.ts pins the [base.fields] empty-enum site, the one of assertNonEmptyEnum's three addressable places that was unpinned, and the one effectiveLifecycleStatusEnum depends on being refused.

Mutation controls, from the delivering note: regressing the fixture to the defect's shape reddens exactly the two carve-out tests; removing the field-spec guard at the code level reddens the pre-existing type-field test and the new [base.fields] test and leaves the items test green. Gates at delivery: bun test 5108 pass / 3 skip / 0 fail, typecheck 0, lint 0, lore check exit 0.

Completed by a later session (2026-10-14) after verifying that f93d5a23 is an ancestor of origin/dev and that the landed tree addresses all three items. The record carried NO acceptance criteria, so nothing was ticked and nothing is left unresolved.
